And his words pleased the Sultan,
and he was prepared to spare Reginald (Raynald of Châtillon),
had not the nobles urged him to kill him.
And they said to him:
"This man does not deserve to live,
for lo, how many times has he sworn and lied!"
Therefore, when he sent both of them to the tent that was prepared for them,
after an hour he sent and brought Reginald to him alone,
and he drew a sword,
and he killed him with his own hands.
For Reginald was an old man who was experienced in wars,
and there was no limit to his strength and his courage,
and he was greatly feared by the Arabs (Tayyaye).
Then Saladin went and encamped against the fortress of Tiberias,
and he persuaded the Queen with oaths and brought her down,
and he sent her to Tripoli along with her people and all her possessions,
and he even gave her gifts besides.
Now the Brethren Templars (Dawwaye) and Hospitallers (Espitalaye),
eighty in number,
who had been taken captive,
he likewise killed;
since he bought most of them from the horsemen,
each brother for five hundred dinars.
For he said:
"These men injure the Arab nation (or Islam) more than all the Franks,
and death is sweet to them because of the triumph of their faith;
therefore let us destroy them."
And from there Saladin came against Acre,
and all the nobles fled by sea to Tyre,
and the poor who remained came out and received a pledge (safe-conduct) for their lives.
And after Acre, they also took Haifa and Nablus,
which is Samaria,
and Tibnin, and Sidon, and Caesarea, and Jaffa, and Beirut, and Nazareth.
And how much mockery and derision the Christians who dwelt in the dominion of the Arabs endured at this time,
speech is unable to encompass.
And the lord of Jubayl (Gibelet),
because he too was a prisoner,
surrendered his city and was delivered.
And Saladin went against Ascalon,
and found it full of warlike men,
and he waged a hard battle against it,
and was not able to subdue it.
Then he said to the lord of Tiberias (to the King of Jerusalem?) who was captive with him,
that if he would surrender Ascalon,
he would release him.
Then the King summoned the governor of Ascalon to him,
and commanded him to surrender it.
